title: Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad

reading.body:
This is a synthetic image edit that reached a public marketing channel, not a model error caught in a draft. A photograph of a real student was altered with AI so that he was replaced by a different person and his classmates were made to appear thinner, and the edited image was placed on banners as a depiction of an actual event. The substitution also changed the student's apparent race, which is how the outlets describe it. The failure sits at the handoff between the editing tool and publication, where the university's own written rules on altering images of its people and events were meant to apply.

Catching it required a review step before the banners went out, because the policy already prohibited using AI to alter images of Stanford people, events, research, facilities or achievements. It also required disclosure, which the university said was missing. Stanford acknowledged the alteration, said both the edit and the lack of disclosure violated its policy, and is working with Residential and Dining Enterprises on additional training and review of materials.

What is not established is intent or who approved the image. The university confirmed the AI alteration and the policy violation, and the student's account of learning about it from a friend is reported, but no finding of deliberate deception has been reported.

reports.title: Stanford Used A.I. to Swap Black Student for Hispanic Student in a Photo
Stanford R&DE Uses AI to Race Swap Students for Advertising
University confirms use of AI-edited photo amid controversy
Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad

summary:
In 2024, a Stanford photographer took a picture of Billy Ramirez, a Hispanic senior majoring in human biology, with two other students at a Lunar New Year party. The university dining service posted the photo online the next day. Last week, Stanford used the image on banners, but Ramirez had been replaced by a Black woman, and the other students were altered to appear thinner. Ramirez learned about it from a friend and said he was upset and frustrated.

Stanford acknowledged on Tuesday that it used artificial intelligence to change the original image. The university said its policy strictly prohibits using AI to produce or alter images of Stanford people, events, research, facilities or achievements. It said the alteration and the lack of disclosure violated that policy. Stanford is working with Residential and Dining Enterprises to provide additional training and ensure proper review of all materials.
